text:
ana: heads up — minimal repro for weird ESM/CJS break on edge runtimes with Vite + our JS SDK. works in node but fails in edge build. :face_with_monocle:

ana: steps i used:
```bash
npx create-vite@latest vite-sdk-edge --template vanilla-ts
cd vite-sdk-edge
yarn add @redwood-inference/sdk
# create a simple edge handler that imports the SDK
# build with vite and run edge dev (esbuild transformer)
```

ana: error seen at runtime in browser/edge bundler: `Uncaught TypeError: Failed to resolve module specifier \"@redwood-inference/sdk\"` and in Next/Edge functions it throws `TypeError: require is not defined` even though package.json has \"type\":\"module\"

david: can you paste the import you used? edge runtimes usually choke on mixed CJS/ESM entry points.

ana: import line is: `import Redwood from '@redwood-inference/sdk'`

ana: SDK package current publish has `main` pointing to dist/index.cjs.js and `module` to dist/index.esm.js, but the `exports` map only includes `.` -> ./dist/index.cjs.js (i think)

mei: that would explain it. bundlers resolve to cjs entry if exports map is incomplete. Edge runtimes often expect ESM only.

sam: also seeing a typing mismatch: our `types` points to `dist/index.d.ts` but the d.ts uses `export = Redwood` style which forces `import x = require()` semantics for TS in ESM projects. breaky.

ana: i put together a tiny repro repo: https://github.com/redwood-internal/devex/vite-sdk-edge-repro (small, shows vite config + failing import).

ci-bot: build failed — vite-sdk-edge-repro / e2e (browser) — 1/3 tests failing (import resolution). Logs:```
Error: Uncaught TypeError: require is not defined at /node_modules/@redwood-inference/sdk/dist/index.cjs.js:1:1
```

david: quick workaround for folks until we fix publish: add a package alias in vite config: `resolve.alias: { '@redwood-inference/sdk': '/node_modules/@redwood-inference/sdk/dist/index.esm.js' }` — ugly but works.

mei: long-term fix options:
- ensure package.json `exports` maps `.` to both `./dist/index.esm.js` (default) and conditional exports for `require` if needed
- make d.ts use `export default` + named exports compatible with ESM consumers
- publish separate `exports` for `import` vs `require` to avoid cjs fallback for ESM bundlers

sam: i can prototype a minimal patch to the types (change to `export default` pattern) and add a small test that imports the package from an ESM-only environment.

ana: that would be huge. for repro clarity, here's the minimal failing file i used in vite project:
```ts
// src/main.ts (vite edge)
import Redwood from '@redwood-inference/sdk'
console.log(Redwood)
```

ana: build output points to the cjs bundle being pulled in by rollup plugin-commonjs during build.

david: could also be that one of our internal deps is CJS-only which triggers commonjs resolution. check `npm ls` for any CJS-only transitive deps.

mei: action items:
- sam: draft types fix + test (ETA 1 day)
- david: look at package.json `exports` map and publish script (ETA today)
- ana: update repro repo with exact `package.json` + minimal vite config and add steps to README (ETA today)

sam: acked, starting on types PR. will ping when draft ready :thumbsup:

ana: thanks. can we also add a short note in SDK docs about bundler pitfalls (vite/webpack/rollup + edge) and recommended package.json fields so users don't hit this?

david: yes — i'll add an entry in the devex docs after we ship the publish fix.

mei: if anyone hits this urgently, use david's alias workaround or import the ESM file path directly from node_modules as a temporary hack.

ana: marking this resolved for now once david patches exports — will reopen thread if regen shows more failures. :eyes:
